title: First-cohomology vanishing of incoming kernels and images for integer complexes
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $V$ an open of $Y$, and $F$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that for every integer $j$ and positive integer $r$, the ordinary sheaf cohomology [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor] of both $\operatorname{coker}(F^{j-1}\to F^j)|_V$ and $H^j(F)|_V$ vanishes in degree $r$. For every integer $p$, the degree-one module right-derived global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] on $V$ of $\ker(F^{p-1}\to F^p)|_V$ and $\operatorname{im}(F^{p-1}\to F^p)|_V$ are zero objects. No boundedness, affineness, quasi-coherence, or termwise vanishing is required.

source.place: Tag 08C2, lemma-alternating-cech-complex-complex-ss, hypotheses (3)(b),(3)(c); Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors, long exact sequence of right derived functors, applied to cycle and opcycle sequences.

proof.text: Convert the ordinary cohomology vanishings into zero objects in module right-derived sections using the natural additive equivalences of lem-sc-module-cohomology-source-comparison on the open subscheme V. Restriction is exact, so the following short exact sequences remain short exact after restriction. Module sheaves on V have enough injectives by lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives, allowing application of the right-derived long exact sequence.

Put $Q^j=\operatorname{coker}d^{j-1}$ and $B^{j+1}=\operatorname{im}d^j$. The right homology kernel property gives $0\to H^j(F)\to Q^j\to B^{j+1}\to0$. Its long exact sequence places $H^1(V,B^{j+1}|_V)$ between $H^1(V,Q^j|_V)=0$ and $H^2(V,H^j(F)|_V)=0$. Hence incoming images have vanishing first cohomology in every degree. The image of the map out of Q identifies with the image of d by its strong epi-mono factorization.

The cycle sequence $0\to B^j\to Z^j\to H^j(F)\to0$ and its long exact sequence put $H^1(V,Z^j|_V)$ between two zero objects, using the preceding step and the homology vanishing hypothesis. Thus cycles have vanishing first cohomology. At degree p, the incoming kernel is $Z^{p-1}$ and the incoming image is $B^p$; transport through the kernel and image universal-property isomorphisms. The argument is valid also for empty V and the zero complex.

proof_origin.place: Direct dimension shifting in the cycle and opcycle short exact sequences; formal proof in IntegerSectionAcyclicIncomingKernelImage.

theorem integer_section_acyclic_incoming_kernel_image
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (F : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) (V : Y.Opens)
    (hcokernels : ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((cokernel (F.d (n - 1) n)).restrict V.ι).H (q + 1)))
    (hhomology : ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ℕ),
      Subsingleton (((F.homology n).restrict V.ι).H (q + 1))) (p : ℤ) :
    IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology V.toScheme.toRingedSpace 1).obj
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (kernel (F.sc p).f))) ∧
    IsZero ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology V.toScheme.toRingedSpace 1).obj
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj (image (F.sc p).f)))
